stories.headline: Nvidia rival Etched exits stealth with working chip, $800M raised and $1B in orders

key_facts.fact: Etched came out of stealth on June 30, announcing a working chip, over $1 billion in signed customer contracts, and a total of $800 million raised across multiple financing rounds.
key_facts.excerpt: Etched, the company building frontier inference clusters, came out of stealth today, announcing a working chip and over $1 billion in signed customer contracts. The company also announced a total of $800M raised across multiple unannounced financing rounds.

key_facts.fact: The latest tranche was a $500 million round that closed in December at a $5 billion post-money valuation, led by Stripes.
key_facts.excerpt: The most recent tranche was an unannounced $500 million round closed in December at a $5 billion post-money valuation, the company said.

key_facts.fact: Backers include VentureTech Alliance (a fund with ties to TSMC), Peter Thiel, Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Jump Trading and Two Sigma, plus angels Andrej Karpathy, Geoffrey Hinton and Fei-Fei Li.
key_facts.excerpt: a strategic investment from VentureTech Alliance, alongside Peter Thiel, Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Jump Trading, Two Sigma, Stripes, Ribbit Capital, Radical Ventures, Primary VC, Positive Sum and AI luminaries including Andrej Karpathy, Geoffrey Hinton, Fei-Fei Li

key_facts.fact: Etched's chip, called Sohu, is designed to run transformer models and achieved first-pass (A0) silicon success on TSMC's N4P process; the company plans to start shipping racks this summer.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's chip, called Sohu, is designed to run transformer models by embedding the architecture directly into silicon rather than relying on general-purpose GPUs... plans to start shipping to customers this summer.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2022 by Harvard dropouts Gavin Uberti and Robert Wachen, Etched spent roughly two years quietly building; Jane Street separately led a previously unannounced round and has invested more than $100 million in total.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2022 by Harvard dropouts Gavin Uberti and Robert Wachen... Jane Street separately led a previously unannounced round and has invested more than $100 million in total, according to Bloomberg.

stories.headline: UBTech launches UWORLD U1, first mass-produced full-size humanoid, priced from 119,800 RMB

key_facts.fact: On June 30, UBTech unveiled the UWORLD U1 Series of full-size ultra-bionic humanoid robots at its 2026 Global Launch Event in Shenzhen, calling it the first in the world designed for mass production.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 30, 2026, UBTECH hosted its 2026 Global Launch Event in Shenzhen... officially unveiled the UWORLD U1 Series of full-size ultra-bionic humanoid robots, the first in the world designed for mass production.

key_facts.fact: The lineup has three models -- the U1 Lite semi-torso edition, the full-body U1 Pro, and the high-dynamic U1 Ultra -- with pricing set from 119,800 RMB.
key_facts.excerpt: The lineup includes three models: the U1 Lite semi-torso edition, the high-performance full-body U1 Pro, and the high-dynamic full-body U1 Ultra, with pricing set from 119,800 RMB.

key_facts.fact: As of the launch day, cumulative orders for the UWORLD U1 Series had surpassed 13,361 units.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the day of the launch event, cumulative orders for the UWORLD U1 Series had surpassed 13,361 units.

key_facts.fact: UBTech ranked first globally in revenue and sales volume from full-size embodied humanoid robots in 2025, and paired the launch with a 'Human-Robot Companionship Initiative' pledging to donate 100 customized U1 units in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: the company ranked 1st globally in revenue and sales volume from full-sized embodied intelligent humanoid robots in 2025... In 2026, UWORLD plans to donate 100 customized U1 Series humanoid robots.

stories.headline: Firmus to build 170,000-GPU Nvidia AI factory in Indonesia, sees $25-30B in offtake

key_facts.fact: Firmus Technologies announced a compute partnership with Nvidia running through 2034, anchored by a 360 MW Nvidia DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus Technologies today announced a strategic compute partnership with NVIDIA running through 2034, anchored by a dedicated 360 MW NVIDIA DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia.

key_facts.fact: The agreement covers up to 170,000 Nvidia AI accelerators across Grace-Blackwell, Vera-Rubin and Vera platforms through 2027 and 2028, among the largest AI infrastructure builds in Asia-Pacific.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement covers up to 170,000 NVIDIA AI accelerators across Grace-Blackwell, Vera-Rubin, and Vera platforms through 2027 and 2028, positioning the Batam campus among the largest AI infrastructure developments in Asia-Pacific.

key_facts.fact: The deal uses a revenue-sharing and credit-support model: Firmus sells Nvidia-powered cloud services and Nvidia earns both product revenue and a share of the cloud revenue on the supported capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus will sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services, with NVIDIA earning both standard product revenue and a share of the cloud revenue on the supported capacity.

key_facts.fact: Firmus expects $25 billion to $30 billion from customer offtake deals in the first six years of the partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus expects to see between $25 billion and $30 billion from customer offtake deals in the first six years of the partnership.

key_facts.fact: The Batam campus is being developed with Singapore-headquartered DayOne and uses Firmus' Australian-designed, liquid-cooled HyperCube architecture.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus' Batam campus is being developed in partnership with DayOne, a Singapore-headquartered global digital infrastructure platform... Firmus' proprietary HyperCube platform, a liquid-cooled AI Factory architecture developed in Australia.

stories.headline: South Korea tops $100B in monthly exports for first time as chip shipments hit record $44.8B

key_facts.fact: South Korea's June exports surged 70.9% year-on-year to $102.25 billion, the first time monthly exports surpassed $100 billion, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources.
key_facts.excerpt: Outbound shipments surged 70.9 percent on-year to $102.25 billion in June, according to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources.

key_facts.fact: Semiconductor exports rose 199.5% year-on-year to a record $44.82 billion, the first time monthly chip exports exceeded $40 billion, beating the prior record of $37.2 billion in May.
key_facts.excerpt: Semiconductor exports rose 199.5 percent from a year earlier to a record $44.82 billion in June. It marked the first time monthly semiconductor exports exceeded $40 billion, surpassing the previous monthly record of $37.2 billion in May.

key_facts.fact: Chips accounted for 43.8% of total export value; the record was driven by SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics meeting unprecedented demand for memory chips amid the AI boom.
key_facts.excerpt: Fueling June's performance were semiconductors, which surged 199.5 percent to $44.8 billion, accounting for 43.8 percent of the value of total exports.

key_facts.fact: The result made Korea only the fourth country to reach $100 billion in monthly exports, after Germany, China and the United States, with a trade surplus above $30 billion for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: making it only the fourth country in the world to reach the milestone, after Germany, China and the United States... the trade surplus topped $30 billion, another historic high.

sources.title: S. Korea's monthly exports hit US$100 bln for 1st time in June
Korea becomes fourth nation to top $100 billion in monthly exports as chip shipments hit record high

stories.headline: ByteDance's $39B Ceará data center confirmed as its largest facility outside China

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is building a roughly $39 billion data center campus at the Pecém port complex in Ceará, Brazil, a project that would rank among the largest single-site infrastructure builds in Latin American history.
key_facts.excerpt: ByteDance is dropping roughly $39 billion on a data center campus in northeastern Brazil, a bet so large it would rank among the most expensive single-site infrastructure projects in Latin American history. The facility, located at the Pecém port complex in the state of Ceará.

key_facts.fact: The campus starts with about 200 MW of IT capacity and 20 data halls (about 300 MW first-phase power demand), designed to scale toward nearly 1 gigawatt; initial operations are expected in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: will start with approximately 200 MW of IT capacity and is designed to scale toward nearly 1 gigawatt. The campus will feature 20 data halls in its initial configuration, with a total power demand near 300 MW for the first phase alone.

key_facts.fact: The total investment exceeds R$200 billion (about $37.7B-$39.9B) and the facility will serve TikTok's operations exclusively outside Brazil, the US, Europe and China.
key_facts.excerpt: The investment totals over R$200 billion, which converts to approximately $37.7 billion to $39.87 billion... The facility is being built exclusively to serve TikTok's operational needs in markets outside Brazil, the US, Europe, and China.

key_facts.fact: The site is developed by Pátria Investimentos-backed Omnia and anchored by a $2 billion renewable-power deal signed with Casa dos Ventos for wind supply from Ceará and Piauí.
key_facts.excerpt: Omnia, the digital infrastructure platform backed by Patria Investments, signed a 20-year renewable energy agreement worth $2 billion with Casa dos Ventos to supply a hyperscale data center linked to ByteDance in Brazil.

stories.headline: Samsung, SK and Amkor pledge $578B for southwest Korea chip hub, targeting double memory capacity

key_facts.fact: Samsung Group, SK Group and Amkor pledged a combined 896 trillion won ($578 billion) to build a chip hub in Korea's southwest, signing an MOU with President Lee Jae Myung in Gwangju on June 30.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung, SK and Amkor pledged a combined investment of 896 trillion won ($578 billion) to establish a chips hub in Korea's southwest... after signing a memorandum of understanding on growing advanced industries in the southwestern region at a convention center in Gwangju on June 30.

key_facts.fact: SK Group pledged 470 trillion won (including SK hynix's 400 trillion won for two memory fabs and a 1-gigawatt AI data center), while Samsung Group pledged 425 trillion won (including 400 trillion won for two fabs in Gwangju plus an AI computing center).
key_facts.excerpt: SK Group pledged to invest 470 trillion won in the southwest region to build two semiconductor fabs, as well as a 1-gigawatt AI data center... Samsung Group will invest 425 trillion won to build two memory fabs, along with an AI computing center in the region.

key_facts.fact: The government unveiled an S-WEST Vision aiming to double South Korea's memory chip production capacity within five years, with Samsung and SK deploying 800 trillion won on four new fabs plus an 81 trillion won packaging hub.
key_facts.excerpt: the two memory giants will jointly deploy 800 trillion won to build four new fabs in the country's southwest, alongside another 81 trillion won dedicated to a semiconductor packaging hub... the South Korean government plans to double domestic DRAM production capacity within five years.

key_facts.fact: Analysts warn the aggressive capex will tighten competition for advanced tools -- EUV, etching, photomask, CMP and deposition -- potentially disrupting TSMC's and Intel's pace of scaling sub-2nm production.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and SK hynix's aggressive capex will tighten competition for key advanced manufacturing tools—including EUV, etching, photomask, CMP, and deposition equipment... The resulting equipment crunch could disrupt TSMC's and Intel's pace of scaling sub-2nm production.

key_facts.fact: Combined with previously announced projects, the two memory makers pledged 3.2 quadrillion won ($2.07 trillion) of investment; SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics shares are up 307% and 179% respectively so far this year.
key_facts.excerpt: the world's two biggest memory chipmakers pledged 3.2 quadrillion won ($2.07 trillion) of investment... Shares of SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics have gone up 307% and 179%, respectively, so far this year.
